header.scope: Online membership billing only. Front-desk/studio processing stays with Global Payments; studios are an undated phase two that depends on the partner integration.
header.tag_why: The paper sat with the controller for two weeks. It was signed four days after Tobi showed which of their own failed renewals were recoverable ('Their file, not our average'). The front-desk single-screen gap 'nearly cost us' and kept the studios out of scope.

messaging_changes.current_line: Proven ROI, backed by an independent economic impact study.
messaging_changes.change: Lead proof with an offer to run the customer's own failed-payment export and show which renewals are recoverable, instead of citing a third-party study.
evidence_excerpts: Greg hadn't said a word in two meetings, and he asked for the spreadsheet.
Then we did the data session, and four days later it was signed.
messaging_changes.why: The silent economic signer engaged only when he saw the proof on their own data, and signature followed within days. Generic ROI did not move a stalled contract.

messaging_changes.current_line: Recover failed payments automatically with smart retries.
messaging_changes.change: Frame recovery as involuntary churn, for example keeping 'members who never meant to leave', tied to the churn number the customer reports to its board.
evidence_excerpts: members who never meant to leave
They report member churn to the board every quarter
messaging_changes.why: The buyer's problem was board-reported churn, not 'failed payments'. Her own phrase names the outcome she cares about.

messaging_changes.current_line: Online and in-store on one platform; the line between them has pretty much disappeared.
messaging_changes.change: Drop the 'unified commerce' framing. Say concretely what the front desk gets (check in and sell on one screen) and be explicit that this runs via a partner integration with the customer's studio software.
messaging_changes.why: The customer heard 'unified commerce' as hardware. The claim that the line has disappeared was not demonstrable in their setup, and that nearly lost the deal.

messaging_changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
messaging_changes.change: Don't open with the global positioning for regional subscription businesses. Open with their churn/recovery problem.
evidence_excerpts: Silence. I opened with the global slide.
messaging_changes.why: For a US-plus-Canada studio chain, the global opener drew silence.

trigger.insight: The trigger was board-level. Churn rose two quarters running, and splitting it showed that failed cards outweighed deliberate cancellations. That made it a revenue-retention problem owned by digital and finance, not a payments-ops problem. The size of the bucket is unverified: the rep explicitly disclaimed 'a third', and the real number sits in Maya's board deck.
trigger.messaging: Position recovery as reducing involuntary churn on the board's metric, and get the actual figure from the deck before reusing it.

decider.insight: The rep first named Maya and changed the answer only under probing. Maya selected the vendor, but Greg the controller held the go/no-go. The deal stalled on him and moved only when he saw numbers. The champion's 'it was my call' masked the economic buyer.
decider.messaging: Write for two audiences: the digital champion and a finance signer who needs customer-specific numbers and contract-exit clarity.

competitor.insight: Global Payments, the incumbent through the studio software, responded by reframing the decision around front-desk hardware and a longer contract. That moved the conversation onto their ground (readers, software compatibility, lock-in) and away from recovery. Greg's repeated termination-fee questions signal that exit cost and lock-in were live concerns. We only know of the offer through Maya; the rep never saw it.
competitor.messaging: Prepare a response to incumbent lock-in bundles: a clear answer on switching and exit costs, and a way to pull the conversation back to recovery value.

message.insight: What landed was customer-specific recovery analysis built from one month of their failed renewals. The global opener got silence. 'Unified commerce' was decoded as hardware, which helped the incumbent's hardware framing. Our language pulled toward the competitor's turf; their data pulled toward ours.
message.messaging: Lead with recovery on their data. Retire the 'unified commerce' jargon and the global opener for this segment.

decided.insight: Until the data session the rep believed we were the stalking horse. The turn came when the silent controller engaged with his own numbers, and signature followed within four days. Value proof in the customer's terms broke the stall.
decided.messaging: Make the 'run your failed-payment file' session a standard step before paper goes to finance, not a rescue move.

gaps.insight: We could not show the reader working inside their studio software (check-in plus retail on one screen). It depends on a partner, and the partner demo was not in their environment. This is why only memberships were signed, the front desk stays with Global, and phase two has no date. The win is partial, and the unified claim is unproven for this account.
gaps.messaging: Don't claim seamless in-store until there is a live, in-environment demo with the studio-software partner. Name the partner dependency honestly.

language.insight: The question was deferred to Slack, so no direct answer exists. Incidental quotes elsewhere show the customer thinks in members and churn ('never meant to leave') and in front-desk staff experience, not in 'payments', 'authorization' or 'unified commerce'.
language.messaging: Hold off on language changes beyond the recovery reframe until the Slack follow-up returns their exact words.

gaps.follow_up: Ask Maya (via the rep) for the actual figure from her board deck.

gaps.follow_up: Track the partner integration status and what the customer needs to see in their own setup to commit.

gaps.follow_up: Ask the rep what we said on exit costs and whether Maya shared any terms of the rate review or terminal bundle.

close.rep_takeaway: Find the signer early. The paper sat with Greg for two weeks while you treated Maya as the decider. Bring finance their own numbers (like Tobi's file analysis) before the contract goes over, and open with their churn problem instead of the global slide.
